checks: Continuity of the original support gap makes Z closed. For Δ≤η the full normal-wise compatibility argument applies unchanged, and on Δ>η the old midpoint support slack is strictly larger than a uniform O(epsilon) source field cost for this fixed η.
The weighted cut fields still satisfy the singleton derivative hypotheses. It gives the two positive endpoint measures and the exact linear cost with χη t and χη(1−t).

Pointwise selection of the lesser of the two Radon–Nikodym densities gives the measurable minimum. Continuous allocations approximate the selector in L1 for their sum measure. Since every cutoff is one on Z, every cost is at least ω(Z). Dominated convergence as η decreases gives the matching infimum.

At polytopal bodies the measure is concentrated on outward facet normals and the overlap on each atom is the smaller actual facet cost. A nonshared facet direction contributes zero, including if active.
Original 72bbac9873894c0b:03 §5 (9)–(11) gives this first-loss formula. The reviewed claim retains the order of fixing a cutoff and only then taking a sufficiently small erosion parameter.

dependencies.mapping: Use one ceiling equal to the original support for each endpoint. The cutoff-weighted fields are jointly continuous, nonnegative and pointwise convex, so the exact normal-pushforward cost follows.
On normals with Δ≤η the cutoff equals one and its normal-wise proof gives the exact midpoint target cut. The slack argument extends it to the other normals.

overlap.comparison: Gives o(t) loss for finitely many nonfacet polytopal truncations, without a continuum shared-normal weighted cost.
Eliminates certain active nonfacet contact multipliers in a finite polyhedral stress chart. It does not derive the exact common-measure overlap for arbitrary convex bodies.

readability: The result is an infimum over cutoff choices and continuous allocations. It does not assert a single globally optimal continuous allocation.
review_method: Independent mathematical proof review of the frozen normalized candidate
summary: For each fixed cutoff the inactive support gap absorbs the source cut. The exact infimum of first endpoint cost is the overlap measure on the active set.
